Work within a range where pain stays at or below 2/10 during the exercise and settles by the next morning.
Sessions A and B alternate; Session C is an optional fourth day in Phase 3 only.
Warm-up every session, 8–10 minutes.
Scapular wall slides to the pain-free limit.
Band external rotation, elbow at side, for maintenance in Phase 2.
Progression: Add 1–2 reps per set each week if pain stays within limits. Increase load only when all sets are completed with good form and no next-morning symptoms.
Introduce finger and grip work in Phase 2: towel hangs on a bar at ground level, plate pinches, and wrist curls. Avoid dead hangs and any hang that loads the shoulder above its current range.
Phase 3: Heavier versions of Phase 2 sessions.
If physio has cleared it, introduce a controlled assisted pull-up or a low-range band pull-down progression in Phase 3.
Session C (optional, 45 min) in Phase 3.

Climbing transition: If the physio clears it, begin bouldering on low-angle, low-height problems. Limit sessions to 30–45 minutes and avoid dynos, deep lock-offs, and heavy overhead reaches in the first two weeks.

Substitutions if pain appears: Pulldown or pull-up → Seated row or band pull-apart; Overhead press → Landmine press (angled, low); Bench press → Push-up on incline; Overhead cable work → Face pull below shoulder height.
Protein: About 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day, spread across 3–4 meals, to support tendon and muscle repair.
Sleep: Aim for 7–9 hours.
Sleep position: Avoid lying on the affected shoulder if it provokes symptoms. A pillow in front of the chest helps.
Desk habits: Break up sitting every 30–45 minutes with 1–2 minutes of thoracic extension and scapular retraction.
Hydration and stress: Both influence pain perception.
Weekly: Log pain score, next-morning symptoms, and sessions completed.
Stop and refer to physio if: night pain, pain that wakes her, numbness or tingling, weakness that worsens, or pain that does not settle within 24 hours of a session.
Reassess at Week 8 and Week 12 with the physio, including range of motion and strength testing.

raw_text:
# 12-Week Upper-Body Programme: Right Subacromial Impingement

## Ground Rules

- **Pain rule:** Work within a range where pain stays at or below 2/10 during the exercise and settles by the next morning. Pain that lingers or increases means reduce load or range.
- **Range limit:** Keep all arm work below the painful arc, typically under shoulder height unless the physio has cleared more. Treat "pain-free range" as a hard boundary.
- **No overhead loading** until the physio clears it in writing. That excludes overhead press, pull-ups, and any loaded arm elevation above shoulder height.
- **Communicate with the physio** before Phase 2 and Phase 3. Share this plan and ask them to confirm the range limits for each phase.
- **Frequency:** 3 sessions per week, with at least one rest day between them. Sessions A and B alternate; Session C is an optional fourth day in Phase 3 only.

## Warm-Up (Every Session, 8–10 minutes)

- Pendulum or arm circles, small diameter, 1 minute
- Band pull-aparts, 2 × 15
- Scapular wall slides, to the pain-free limit, 2 × 10
- Thoracic extension over a foam roller or chair back, 1 minute
- Band external rotation, elbow at side, 2 × 15

## Phase 1: Weeks 1–4 (Calm Down and Build Control)

**Goal:** Restore scapular control, rotator cuff endurance, and thoracic mobility. Keep the shoulder calm.

**Session A:**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Band external rotation (elbow at side) | 3 × 15 | Tempo 3-1-3 |
| Prone Y/T raises (light or bodyweight) | 3 × 10 each | Stay below shoulder height |
| Seated cable row (neutral grip) | 3 × 10–12 | Light load, squeeze shoulder blades |
| Chest-supported dumbbell row | 3 × 10–12 | Elbow path close to the body |
| Goblet squat or leg press | 3 × 10 | Lower-body balance work |
| Dead bug or Pallof press | 3 × 10/side | Trunk stability |

**Session B:**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Side-lying external rotation | 3 × 12 | Light dumbbell, 1–2 kg |
| Scapular push-up (plank position) | 3 × 10 | Protraction focus |
| Neutral-grip lat pulldown to upper chest | 3 × 10–12 | Keep elbows below shoulder level |
| Machine chest press (neutral grip, under shoulder height) | 3 × 10 | Reduce range if pain appears |
| Romanian deadlift (light) | 3 × 10 | Hip hinge pattern |
| Side plank (knees down if needed) | 3 × 20 sec/side | Trunk and shoulder stability |

**Session C (Phase 3 only)** is described below.

**Progression:** Add 1–2 reps per set each week if pain stays within limits. Increase load only when all sets are completed with good form and no next-morning symptoms.

## Phase 2: Weeks 5–8 (Build Strength in Safe Range)

**Goal:** Build loaded pulling and pressing strength within the cleared range and begin lower-level climbing-specific work.

**Session A:**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Single-arm dumbbell row | 4 × 8–10/side | Brace the trunk |
| Seated cable row (neutral grip) | 3 × 10 | Progress load |
| Incline dumbbell press (≤30°, under shoulder height) | 3 × 8–10 | Stop at comfortable depth |
| Cable face pull (to forehead, below shoulder height) | 3 × 12–15 | Rear delt and cuff |
| Band external rotation, elbow at side | 3 × 15 | Maintenance |
| Farmer's carry | 3 × 30 m | Grip and trunk |

**Session B:**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Lat pulldown (neutral grip, to chest) | 4 × 8–10 | Progress load |
| Push-up (floor or incline) | 3 × 8–12 | Stop at pain-free depth |
| Dumbbell pullover (light, range monitored) | 3 × 10 | Check physio clearance first |
| Cable lateral raise (below shoulder height) | 3 × 12 | Light load |
| Single-arm cable row, half-kneeling | 3 × 10/side | Anti-rotation |
| Hollow body hold or hanging knee raise (no hang) | 3 × 20–30 sec | Trunk for climbing |

**Climbing Note:** Introduce finger and grip work now: towel hangs on a bar at ground level, plate pinches, and wrist curls. Avoid dead hangs and any hang that loads the shoulder above its current range.

## Phase 3: Weeks 9–12 (Return Toward Climbing Demands)

**Goal:** Build pulling capacity and climbing-relevant endurance. Test whether the shoulder tolerates more demanding positions, but only with physio approval.

**Physio checkpoint (end of Week 8):** Confirm whether overhead or hanging work is cleared. If not, continue with the Phase 2 range limits and use the substitutions below.

**Session A:** Heavier versions of Phase 2 Session A, with 4 × 6–8 on rows and cable work.

**Session B:** Heavier versions of Phase 2 Session B. If physio has cleared it, introduce a **controlled assisted pull-up** or a **low-range band pull-down** progression.

**Session C (optional, 45 min):**

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Ring or TRX row (feet progressively elevated) | 4 × 8–10 | Pull within pain-free range |
| Dumbbell bench press (neutral grip) | 3 × 8 | Stay below shoulder height |
| Grip circuit: towel hang, plate pinch, reverse wrist curl | 3 rounds | Forearm endurance |
| Core circuit: Pallof press, dead bug, side plank | 3 rounds | Trunk |
| Light bike or rower | 10 min | Conditioning |

**Climbing Transition:** If the physio clears it, begin bouldering on low-angle, low-height problems. Limit sessions to 30–45 minutes and avoid dynos, deep lock-offs, and heavy overhead reaches in the first two weeks.

## Substitutions if Pain Appears

| Painful movement | Substitute |
|---|---|
| Pulldown or pull-up | Seated row or band pull-apart |
| Overhead press | Landmine press (angled, low) |
| Bench press | Push-up on incline |
| Overhead cable work | Face pull below shoulder height |

## Nutrition and Recovery

- **Protein:** About 1.6–2.2 g/kg bodyweight per day, spread across 3–4 meals, to support tendon and muscle repair.
- **Sleep:** Aim for 7–9 hours. Tendon adaptation and pain sensitivity both worsen with poor sleep.
- **Sleep position:** Avoid lying on the affected shoulder if it provokes symptoms. A pillow in front of the chest helps.
- **Desk habits:** Break up sitting every 30–45 minutes with 1–2 minutes of thoracic extension and scapular retraction. Set the monitor at eye level and keep the keyboard close to avoid reaching.
- **Hydration and stress:** Both influence pain perception. Keep them in mind when reviewing her progress.

## Review Points

- **Weekly:** Log pain score, next-morning symptoms, and sessions completed.
- **Stop and refer to physio if:** night pain, pain that wakes her, numbness or tingling, weakness that worsens, or pain that does not settle within 24 hours of a session.
- **Reassess at Week 8 and Week 12** with the physio, including range of motion and strength testing.
